title: GPU Bring-Up Field Manual
intro_html: 50 hands-on tasks from a first triage script to a full cluster validation kit. Every task has steps, a deliverable, verified GitHub repos, docs and an interview question. It is built around the actual posting: bring-up and validation, RDMA, NCCL, PCIe and NUMA, BMC and Redfish, Linux depth, hyperscaler knowledge.
lead_html: The posting asks for people who have brought up large GPU platforms and can explain what is wrong when a cluster underperforms. A cloud architect with Terraform, Kubernetes and multi-team delivery experience already has part of that. The gaps are the hardware and fabric layers, and those are what most of this manual trains.
time_html: Time. The full path is 471 hours, about 21 hours a week for 22 weeks. The Core path subset (26 tasks, 233 hours, about 11 hours a week) keeps every area of the posting. Pick it if you are working full time.

notes.title: Where you stand, from what you told me
notes.html:
Strong: Linux and containers, Kubernetes (CKAD), IaC, hyperscaler compute and networking, customer delivery across teams.

Gaps to close: hands-on GPU diagnostics, RDMA and NCCL, PCIe/NUMA/BIOS, BMC and Redfish, bare-metal provisioning.

LinkedIn blocked my access, so this is not a profile review. Paste your profile text for a line-by-line one.

notes.title: Lab tiers, so cost stays low
notes.html:
• Tier 0: laptop or one VM. Soft-RoCE, Redfish mockups, OpenBMC in QEMU, Slurm in Docker, KWOK fake GPU nodes.
  • Tier 1: one GPU instance on spot.
  • Tier 2: one multi-GPU node.
  • Tier 3: two or more EFA or InfiniBand nodes for a few hours. Tear down every night.

notes.title: What the call changed
notes.html:
From a mentoring conversation with an NVIDIA Sr. Solutions Architect (AI Inference): learn LLM basics at a light level, go deep on how workloads are deployed on Kubernetes, think about storage close to compute, topology-aware GPU placement, Kubernetes security (admission policy), CRDs and operators, NVIDIA's free courses.

Her role is inference-focused. The Infrastructure posting is closer to hardware bring-up, so those items became H4, H5, H7, H8, I3 and K1 to K4, and the hardware tasks (C, D, E) were added on top.

notes.title: How I checked this
notes.html: Every GitHub repo linked here was confirmed to exist with a readable README on Oct 8, 2026. Star counts are omitted because I could not verify them live. Doc figures (DCGM durations, XID meanings, NCP-AII weights, the 92% all-reduce bar) were read from the cited pages. Where a command or flag varies by version, the task says to check the README.

footer: Built Oct 8, 2026. Re-check hardware-specific commands against your driver, CUDA and NCCL versions before relying on a number.
